title: Toby and the Sleepy Star
markdown:
There once was a tiny bear named Toby. He was no bigger than your thumb. His fur was the colour of warm honey. Toby lived with Nell, a kitten made of soft white fluff. Her paws felt like dandelion seeds. They slept in a mossy bed. It was right by a window. The window looked out onto the big world.

One soft morning, Toby and Nell woke up. The sky was pale blue. Toby stretched his tiny arms. Nell did a little fluffy yawn.

“Lovely morning,” purred Nell. Her voice was like a tiny breeze.

Toby looked out the window. And there it was. On the dewy grass sat a little star. But this star was yawning. It made a soft sleepy aaaah sound. Its sparkles looked droopy.

“Oh dear,” said Toby. His nose twitched. “The little star looks sad. It should be in the sky, not here alone.”

Nell blinked her big blue eyes. “How did it get here?”

“I don’t know,” whispered Toby. “But we must help it get back before breakfast. Mama Bear says breakfast is very important.”

Toby was a very tiny bear. The sky looked very, very big. A little flutter started in Toby’s tummy. His whiskers drooped. His tummy felt like wobbly jelly. “Oh dear,” he thought. “This is too big for me.”

Nell nudged him. Her fluffy tail gave a little swish. “Come on, Toby. We have to try. If we don’t help the star, it will get all dim and won’t shine for anyone.” The thought of the star losing its sparkle made Toby’s heart feel a little squeeze.

The sun was painting the sky pink at the edges. If the star wasn’t home now, it would be too bright for it to go.

So Toby took a deep breath. He and Nell climbed carefully out of their window. Their little feet landed on the cool damp grass. The little star gave another slow yawn. Its light was soft and silvery. As they tiptoed closer, Toby could feel a faint warm hum.

They padded over to the star. It felt warm and a little wobbly. The world felt quiet. Toby’s tummy fluttered again. The sky indeed seemed to stretch on forever.

“Hmm, how will we get you up, little star?” Nell meowed softly. The star just gave a little sigh.

Just then, a friendly moonbeam stretched from the sky to the grass. It was like a silver ribbon. “Hello, little ones,” chimed the moonbeam. Its voice was like a tinkling bell. “I see you have a little star who needs a lift. But it seems sleepy and heavy. Perhaps it misses its friends.”

Nell purred. “It’s tired. Toby thinks we should sing to it.”

Toby nodded. He thought of stars he’d seen at night, all twinkling and dancing. He remembered a soft humming song. He imagined the star feeling happy and light, dancing with its friends.

“Twinkle, twinkle, little star,” Toby began. His voice was a tiny squeak, but clear and sweet.
Nell joined in, a soft purring hum that felt like a warm hug.
“How I wonder what you are.”
As they sang, their voices weaving together, the little star stopped yawning. Its droopy sparkles perked up, shining with a soft steady glow. It felt lighter, bobbing up and down gently.

“Oh, wonderful,” exclaimed the moonbeam. Its silvery light shone brighter. “It feels much lighter now. Ready to go home.”

The moonbeam lifted them, like a gentle elevator made of pure light. But as they rose higher, the wind began to whisper. It was a whoosh and a swish. Toby’s little paws felt wobbly. He hesitated. He would have to let go of Nell’s soft paw, the one that always felt so safe and warm. His paws felt prickly with worry. The wind tugged at his fur, and the distant ground looked so far, far away. But the little star needed him. He took a deep breath and let go, reaching instead for the moonbeam’s edge. The sudden feeling of being alone, even for a moment, made his tummy do a flip-flop.

Nell nudged him, a warm fluffy presence. “It’s okay, Toby,” she purred, her purr a steady rumble of comfort. “We’re together. The moonbeam is holding us safe.” Toby opened his eyes and saw Nell’s calm steady gaze. He felt a little steadier.

The moonbeam, seeing Toby’s wobbly paws, began to descend softly. It swooped them down, down, down, through the whispering air, landing them softly back near their window. The little star, now bright and cheerful, gave a final happy twinkle. Then it floated up, up, up, joining its star friends in the brightening sky, where it twinkled with all its might.

Mama Bear was stirring inside. “Breakfast time,” she called, her voice warm and welcoming.

Toby and Nell climbed back through the window. The first golden rays of sunshine peeked over the hills. Toby looked up at the sky. He saw no sign of the little star, but he knew it was there, shining brightly. That fluttery worry in his tummy? It was gone. Replaced by a warm happy feeling, like a little sunbeam inside him.

Later, Toby looked out the window at the tall trees. They were so high. But he didn’t feel worried. “Wow, those trees are tall,” he said. “But I’m not scared. I was brave for the star.”

He sat down to breakfast with Nell, honey on his paws, and the sky outside looking just a little brighter for having its star back.
